new_statements.quote: Momuna phonemes are orthographically symbolised as follows: the stops t, k, b; the liquid r; the sibilant s; the nasals m, n; the semi-vowels w, y; the labialised stops bw, kw; the palatalised consonants sy, by, ny; the vowels i, ee (close mid front), e (open mid front), a, o (low back), oo (close mid back), u; the diphthongs ei, ai, oi, au, ou. There are three levels of contrastive tone on monosyllables: high (marked by the acute accent), mid (unmarked) and low (marked by a grave accent). On non-monosyllabic words only two levels are contrastive, and these on the stressed syllable only.
new_statements.citation: Reimer, Martha. 1986. The notion of topic in Momuna narrative discourse. In Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 25 (Pacific Linguistics A-74), 181-204. Canberra: Research School of Pacific and Asian Studies, Australian National University.
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: QUOTE: Opened (24 pp., sealang PL-A74 pp.181-204, text present) and rendered pp. 21-22 (printed pp. 201-202) to images. Note 1 reads exactly as quoted: '..There are three levels of contrastive tone on monosyllables: high (marked by the acute accent), mid (unmarked) and low (marked by a grave accent). On non-monosyllabic words only two levels are contrastive, and these on the stressed syllable only.' (the scanned has '5' for s and '0/00' for o/oo, but the page scan matches the report's wording verbatim). READING: agree with tone language with a stress statement for the passage itself: lexical tone (3 levels on monosyllables, 2 on polysyllables) with the contrast confined to 'the stressed syl…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Momuna (the language the spurious 'Momina' entry duplicates) is described as having lexical tone: three levels on monosyllables, but in polysyllabic words only a two-way tone contrast, realised on the stressed syllable alone. The note presupposes one stressed syllable per word but does not state where it falls or whether its position is predictable.
new_statements.exceptions: None; the note is an orthographic/phonemic footnote in a discourse paper, not a phonology.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level (monosyllabic vs non-monosyllabic words); tone marks in the paper's transcription. Stress location itself is left unstated, so no positional reading can be assigned; the system as described (tone contrast restricted to the stressed syllable) is compatible with a pitch accent/culminative-tone analysis.
new_statements.identity_note: Current Glottolog files momi1242 under Bookkeeping: 'The Momina [mmb] entry is spurious, and the result of a misinterpretation (p.c. Dick Kroneman 2025) of a cautiously formulated survey by Kroneman and Peckham 1989'; Samboga village lies inside Momuna [mqf] territory and 'there is only one language in this territory' (Henson 2003:177-180). Waelchli 2025:433 likewise: 'I am not aware of any documentation of a separate language Momina. Henson (1988) on Momina spirit cosmology treats Momuna.' Every linguistic statement found therefore describes Momuna (momu1241, ISO mqf; Reimer's data from Sumo on the Balim/Vriendschap River), which is a separate target in this compilation. The quoted statement should be filed under momu1241, not as a second entity.
